- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses mean reversion; if 10-day average price is > 78, forecast should not exceed 82 unless sentiment >0.7.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” trap.
- When sentiment is 1.0 for 2+ consecutive days, model tends to overforecast; apply 2–4% downward correction unless price is already near 82+.
